This funnel now matches mine at every stage — the cross-environment divergence is resolved. Candidate pool: IDENTICAL (298/298). Correlation-pruning survivors (kept_corr): IDENTICAL (191/191). Quick-XGBoost importance top-60: 60/60 identical — this used to be the exact point of divergence (39–42/60 in earlier runs); it's now a full match after pinning colsample_bytree=1.0, subsample=1.0 and tree_method="exact" in the screening model. VIF pruning removed the same IDENTICAL — 6 features, in the same order, at the same VIF values (including the one exact singularity, avg_occupancy_7d, vif=inf on both machines) — this was the last gap, caused by your statsmodels 0.14.5 not internally standardizing before computing VIF the way my 0.15.0 silently did; prune_vif() now standardizes explicitly so it no longer depends on which statsmodels version is installed. Final feature set: IDENTICAL (51 features, both runs).

The only remaining difference is in the final model's tuned hyperparameters (Optuna's 30-trial search landing on a different point each time it's run — this was never claimed to be deterministic, only the pruning funnel was): your run got R²=0.9792, MAE=$2.88; mine got R²=0.9790, MAE=$2.86 — both well within normal search-to-search noise on the same 51-feature set.
Correlation with the target and multicollinearity among features are different things. ADR_Discount_Pct has one of the strongest target-correlations of anything in the whole 298-feature pool (r=−0.945) yet gets cut at the VIF stage — because a handful of other surviving features jointly reconstruct most of its variance even though no single one of them pairwise-correlates with it above 0.85.
